featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve visited this restaurant a few times, and it consistently has a queue, likely due to its compact size and popularity. Since we were a group of 10, finding comfortable seating was a bit challenging.
One of the highlights is that they serve food without onion and garlic, which is great for Jain guests. We ordered a starter, a couple of sabzis, roti, dal, and biryani—the taste was decent overall.

It works well as a quick dining option if you don’t have many alternatives, but for a calm and relaxed meal, you may want to consider other places.

featured_reviews.name: Amhi Kalakaar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Shree Krishna Restaurant, and my experience was nothing short of comforting. Sometimes, all you want is a simple, satisfying Indian meal that feels like home — and that’s exactly what I found here. I ordered Dal Khichdi and Chaas, and it turned out to be the perfect choice for a wholesome, light yet fulfilling lunch.

The Dal Khichdi was cooked to perfection — soft, balanced in spices, and full of that comforting aroma of ghee and dal. It wasn’t too oily or heavy, and every bite felt nourishing and fresh. The texture was just right, neither too thick nor watery, and you could tell it was made with care, not hurriedly thrown together.

The Chaas (buttermilk) complemented it beautifully. It was chilled, perfectly salted, and had that lovely hint of jeera that makes it so refreshing. Together, the khichdi and chaas made for a meal that instantly lifted my mood — simple, traditional, and soul-satisfying.

The restaurant itself has a clean, no-fuss setup with prompt service and polite staff. I really appreciated how quickly the food was served and how humble the overall atmosphere felt. It’s not a fancy dining place, but it’s one of those hidden gems where taste, simplicity, and satisfaction truly stand out.

If you’re craving homely comfort food, I’d highly recommend trying Shree Krishna Restaurant’s Dal Khichdi and Chaas combo — it’s comfort in its purest form!

Visited Banana Leaf Restaurant at Golden Nest Bhayandar today. Honestly, the experience did not match the hype. We added our name to the waiting list, waited around 45 minutes, and then watched another party get seated before us despite our name already being registered. That kind of poor queue management immediately sets a bad tone.

Food was mixed. Dosa was decent, chutneys were the best part of the meal, and sambar was average. But the button idlis were disappointing — lacked freshness, texture, and overall taste. For a place known for South Indian food, idlis should be a basic strength.

I visited this restaurant with high expectations, but unfortunately, the overall experience was extremely disappointing due to the poor service.
We placed an order for Masala Papad, Spring Roll, and Cheese Ball Dry at 8:48 PM. Despite multiple reminders, the Masala Papad was served only at 9:21 PM. Waiting over 30 minutes for a simple Masala Papad was already concerning, especially when the restaurant was not particularly busy.
The Cheese Ball Dry arrived at 9:45 PM, nearly an hour after ordering. Later, we ordered Khoya Kaju and 3 Rotis, which were served at 10:02 PM. We specifically requested that the curry not be sweet, and the staff assured us it would be prepared spicy.
Meanwhile, we kept following up regarding the Spring Roll, which had still not arrived. To our surprise, we were informed that the order had never been communicated to the kitchen. It was difficult to believe that after nearly an hour, such a basic oversight had occurred.
What made the situation worse was the staff's response. Instead of apologizing, a service staff member casually suggested cancelling the Spring Roll order and was smiling while doing so. There seemed to be little concern for the inconvenience caused or respect for the customer's time.
As we were about to settle the bill, the Spring Roll finally arrived at 10:30 PM—almost 1 hour and 45 minutes after the order was placed. By then, it was too late to make up for the poor experience.
The food may have been acceptable, but the service was among the worst I have experienced. Excessive delays, poor communication, lack of coordination with the kitchen, and an indifferent attitude towards customers made the entire visit frustrating.
I would not recommend this place based on my experience. The management seriously needs to improve its service standards and customer handling.
